# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Osborne_2025_lidocaine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Osborne_2025_lidocaine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s13318-025-00948-1> (open access; the
  electronic supplementary material holds the final NM-TRAN code for the PK
  model, supplementary model code 1, and for the PD model, supplementary model
  code 2)

Osborne and colleagues modelled unbound and total lidocaine after a 2 mg/kg
bolus and a 1.5 mg/kg/h infusion given either intraperitoneally or
intravenously for up to 72 h after laparoscopic colon resection. The packaged
model joins the paper's two NONMEM models. The PK model has unbound lidocaine,
the AAG turnover and the total-lidocaine binding layer. The PD model fixed the
unbound PK and added the resting VAS pain score. The PK block is the same in
both, so all four outputs come from one model:

| Output | Meaning | Units |
|---|---|---|
| `Cunbound` | unbound plasma lidocaine, `central / vc` | mg/L |
| `Cc` | total plasma lidocaine, `Cunbound / fu` with `fu = 1 / (1 + aag / kaag)` | mg/L |
| `aag` | plasma alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (an ODE state) | umol/L |
| `score` | VAS pain score at rest | cm (0-10) |

Intraperitoneal doses go to `depot_ip` and intravenous doses to `central`.
Time 0 is the start of lidocaine, just before surgical dissection, and is also
when the surgical stimulus on AAG synthesis is largest. The `T_SURG` covariate
(duration of surgery, h) starts the natural-history pain-resolution clock, and
`PAGE` (postmenstrual age, weeks) feeds the AAG maturation function, which is 1
for any adult.

# Population

The lidocaine data come from 56 adults in a double-blind RCT of
intraperitoneal versus intravenous lidocaine during and after elective
laparoscopic colon resection in Auckland, New Zealand (NCT03105193; 28 per
arm). Median age was 74 years (range 57-89) in the intraperitoneal arm and 68
years (45-84) in the intravenous arm (Osborne 2025 Table 1). Both arms received
a 2 mg/kg bolus (maximum 100 mg), dosed on ideal body weight, followed by
1.5 mg/kg/h by the same route for up to 72 h. In total, 388 unbound and 388
total concentrations and 275 resting VAS scores were analysed. The AAG
sub-model was fitted to 210 AAG concentrations from 141 children after major
surgery (Booker 1996, Linnarsson 2023; supplementary Table S1). The natural
history of pain also used 17 mean placebo-arm pain scores from adults after
laparoscopic colectomy or cholecystectomy. The paper does not report body
weight or sex.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Osborne_2025_lidocaine")()$population`.

# Source trace

The final THETA, OMEGA and SIGMA values of supplementary model code 1 (PK) and
code 2 (PD) agree with Tables 2 and 3 of the paper. Where the code carries
more digits, the code value is used.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `ltabs` (absorption half-life) | 0.543 h | Code 1 `POP_TABS_IP`; Table 2 t1/2abs 0.54 h |
| `lfdepot` (fraction of IP dose reaching plasma) | 0.664 | Code 1 `POP_FFPM`; Table 2 F 0.66 |
| `lcl`, `lvc`, `lq`, `lvp` | 121 L/h, 103 L, 195 L/h, 555 L (per 70 kg) | Table 2 CLU, V1, Q, V2 |
| `lvip` | 0.1 L/70 kg, held constant | Table 2 VIP; Methods |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_tabs` | 0.75, 1, 0.25 | Supplementary Methods 1 Eq. 11; code 1 `FSZCL`, `FSZV`, `FSZT` |
| `lkin_aag` | 0.0579 umol/h/70 kg | Code 1 `POP_RATEIN`; Table 2 RATEIN_AAG 0.058 |
| `lcl_aag` | 0.00627 L/h/70 kg | Table 2 CL_AAG |
| `lvc_aag` | 3.5 L/70 kg, held constant | Table 2 V_AAG |
| `lthalf_stim` | 34.64 h | Table 2 t1/2 |
| `lslope_stim` | 11.9 | Code 1 `POPSLOPE`; Table 2 Slope 12 |
| `lkaag` (KD) | 2.98 umol/L | Table 2 KD |
| `ltm50_kin_aag`, `lhill_kin_aag` | 32 weeks, 8.94; held constant | Code 1 `POPPMA50`, `POPHILL` |
| `le0` | 10 cm, held constant | Table 3 E0 |
| `lec50` | 0.206 mg/L, held constant | Code 2 `POP_C50`; Table 3 C50 0.21 |
| `logitemax` | logit(0.593) | Code 2 `POP_EMAX` (logit-transformed); Table 3 Emax 0.59 |
| `lhill` | 4 | Table 3 HILL |
| `lemax_pain`, `lhill_pain`, `lt50_pain` | 0.983 (held constant), 0.33, 16.3 h | Code 2; Table 3 Emax,PAIN, HILLPAIN, T50,PAIN |
| PK IIV block (TABS, CLU, V1, Q, V2) | see model file | Code 1 `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)`; Table 2 %PPV = sqrt(omega) x 100 |
| `etalkin_aag + etalcl_aag` | 0.15, 0.261, 0.513 | Code 1 `$OMEGA BLOCK(2)` |
| `etaltm50_kin_aag` | 0.018, held constant | Code 1 `PPVPMA50` |
| `etalec50`, `etalogitemax`, `etalhill_pain`, `etalt50_pain` | 0.255, 0.470, 0.074, 9.89 | Code 2 `$OMEGA`; Table 3 %PPV |
| `propSd`, `addSd` (total) | 0.271, 0.0419 mg/L | Code 1 `CV_LTOT`, `SD_LTOT` |
| `propSd_Cunbound`, `addSd_Cunbound` | 0.26, 0.0304 mg/L | Code 1 `CV_LUN`, `SD_LUN` |
| `propSd_aag` | sqrt(0.0372) | Code 1 `$SIGMA` ERRCV (variance) |
| `propSd_score`, `addSd_score` | 0.462, 0.127 cm | Code 2 `CV_PDE`, `SD_PDE` |
| `ka = log(2) / tabs` | n/a | Methods Eq. 1 |
| IP loss: `d/dt(central) <- fdepot * ka * depot_ip - ...` | n/a | Code 1 `DADT(1)`, `DADT(2)` |
| `d/dt(aag) <- (kin_aag * syn - cl_aag * aag) / vc_aag` | n/a | Methods Eq. 2; code 1 `DADT(4)` |
| `syn <- 1 + slope_stim * exp(-log(2) / thalf_stim * t)` | n/a | Methods Eqs. 3-4; code 1 `$DES` |
| `aag(0) <- kin_aag / cl_aag` | n/a | Code 1 `AAG0`, `A_0(4)` |
| `fmat` (Hill maturation on PMA) | n/a | Methods Eq. 5; code 1 `FMAT` |
| `fu <- 1 / (1 + aag / kaag)`, `Cc <- Cunbound / fu` | n/a | Methods Eqs. 6-7 |
| `score <- e0 * (1 - pain_res) * (1 - drug_eff)` | n/a | Methods Eqs. 8-10; code 2 `EFX` |
| `tpost <- max(t - T_SURG, 0)` | n/a | Code 2 `TNOW = TIME - DURATION` |

# Virtual cohort

The original data are not public. The cohort below has 150 virtual adults per
arm. Neither weight nor height is reported, so these are assumed (see
Assumptions). Doses follow the trial protocol: a 2 mg/kg ideal-body-weight
bolus capped at 100 mg, then 1.5 mg/kg/h ideal body weight for 72 h, both by
the arm's route.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20251)
n_per_arm <- 150

# Observation grid: the trial's sampling times (0.08, 0.5, 1, 2, 6, 12, 48 h)
# plus a denser grid for the VPC panels.
pk_times <- c(0.08, 0.5, 1, 2, 6, 12, 48)
grid_times <- sort(unique(c(0, pk_times, 0.25, 1.5, 3, 4, 8, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 54, 60, 66, 72)))
t_surg <- 3 # assumed operative time (h); starts the pain-resolution clock
pain_times <- t_surg + c(2, 6, 24, 48, 72) # VAS scheduled 2-72 h postoperatively

make_cohort <- function(n, arm, id_offset) {
  sexf <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  ht <- ifelse(sexf == 1, rnorm(n, 162, 6), rnorm(n, 176, 7))
  # Devine ideal body weight (kg) from height (cm)
  ibw <- ifelse(sexf == 1, 45.5, 50) + 0.9055 * (ht - 152.4)
  age <- if (arm == "IP") runif(n, 57, 89) else runif(n, 45, 84)
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 80, 15), 45), 140),
    PAGE = 52.18 * age + 40,
    T_SURG = t_surg,
    ibw = ibw
  )
  dose_cmt <- if (arm == "IP") "depot_ip" else "central"
  bolus <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = pmin(2 * ibw, 100), rate = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = dose_cmt)
  infusion <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = 1.5 * ibw * 72, rate = 1.5 * ibw, evid = 1L, cmt = dose_cmt)
  # `aag` is both an ODE state and a declared endpoint, so observation rows
  # sit on it; every other output is still returned on these rows.
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = sort(unique(c(grid_times, pain_times)))) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "aag")
  bind_rows(bolus, infusion, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_per_arm, "IP", id_offset = 0L),
  make_cohort(n_per_arm, "IV", id_offset = n_per_arm)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Osborne_2025_lidocaine")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("arm"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

# Typical-value checks

The baseline AAG concentration is the turnover steady state
`kin_aag / cl_aag` = 0.0579 / 0.00627 = 9.23 umol/L for a 70 kg adult. Under a
constant infusion, unbound lidocaine approaches the closed-form steady state
`F * R / CL`. Here F is 0.664 for the intraperitoneal route and 1 for the
intravenous route.

```{r typical}
typ_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.01), seq(12, 72, by = 0.25), 200)))
typ_solve <- function(rate_mgkgh, route = "depot_ip", wt = 70, t_end = 72) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 100, cmt = route, time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = rate_mgkgh * wt * t_end, rate = rate_mgkgh * wt, cmt = route, time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(typ_times, cmt = "aag")
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, ev,
    params = c(WT = wt, PAGE = 52.18 * 50 + 40, T_SURG = 0),
    omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    mutate(rate_mgkgh = rate_mgkgh)
}

# Long infusion (t_end = 200 h) to compare the 200 h value with the closed form
ss_ip <- typ_solve(2, t_end = 200)
ss_iv <- typ_solve(2, route = "central", t_end = 200)
cl_typ <- 121
css_ip <- 0.664 * 2 * 70 / cl_typ
css_iv <- 2 * 70 / cl_typ
aag0 <- ss_ip$aag[ss_ip$time == 0]
c200_ip <- ss_ip$Cunbound[ss_ip$time == 200]
c200_iv <- ss_iv$Cunbound[ss_iv$time == 200]

data.frame(
  Check = c("AAG at time 0 (umol/L)", "Unbound Css, IP 2 mg/kg/h (mg/L)", "Unbound Css, IV 2 mg/kg/h (mg/L)"),
  Expected = c(0.0579 / 0.00627, css_ip, css_iv),
  Simulated = c(aag0, c200_ip, c200_iv)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

stopifnot(
  # Same parameters on both sides: pure numerical error.
  abs(aag0 / (0.0579 / 0.00627) - 1) < 1e-6,
  # 200 h is about 9 terminal half-lives, so the infusion is at steady state.
  abs(c200_ip / css_ip - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(c200_iv / css_iv - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# Replicate Figure 4

Figure 4 of the paper shows a 70 kg adult given a 100 mg intraperitoneal bolus
followed by an intraperitoneal infusion. Panels A-B use 1, 1.5, 2 or
2.5 mg/kg/h. Panels C-D show unbound lidocaine, total lidocaine and AAG for
the 2 mg/kg/h regimen. The surgery-to-pain clock is started at time 0
(`T_SURG = 0`).

```{r figure-4ab, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
fig4 <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 1.5, 2, 2.5), typ_solve)) |>
  filter(time <= 72)

fig4 |>
  select(time, rate_mgkgh, `Unbound lidocaine (mg/L)` = Cunbound, `Pain score (VAS cm)` = score) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(time, rate_mgkgh)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = factor(rate_mgkgh))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = "IP infusion\n(mg/kg/h)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 panels A-B of Osborne 2025 (typical 70 kg adult, 100 mg IP bolus)."
  )
```

```{r figure-4cd, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
fig4 |>
  filter(rate_mgkgh == 2) |>
  select(time, `Unbound (mg/L)` = Cunbound, `Total (mg/L)` = Cc, `AAG (umol/L)` = aag) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, linetype = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 panels C-D of Osborne 2025 (2 mg/kg/h IP infusion)."
  )
```

The paper's Results give two times for the 5-point pain reduction: 1.3 h at
1 mg/kg/h and about 36 min at 2 mg/kg/h. The paper links that reduction to the
unbound C50 of 0.21 mg/L. Both readings are tabulated below: the time unbound
lidocaine first reaches 0.21 mg/L, and the time the pain score first falls to
5. The panel C-D values at 72 h were read off Figure 4D by the maintainers.

```{r figure-4-times}
t_first <- function(time, x, thr, below = FALSE) {
  hit <- if (below) x <= thr else x >= thr
  min(time[hit])
}
fig4_times <- fig4 |>
  group_by(rate_mgkgh) |>
  summarise(
    t_c50 = t_first(time, Cunbound, 0.21),
    t_score5 = t_first(time, score, 5, below = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(paper = c(1.3, NA, 0.6, NA))

fig4_times |>
  rename(
    "IP infusion (mg/kg/h)" = rate_mgkgh,
    "Time to unbound 0.21 mg/L (h)" = t_c50,
    "Time to pain score 5 (h)" = t_score5,
    "Paper, Results text (h)" = paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

d72 <- fig4 |> filter(rate_mgkgh == 2, time == 72)
data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Unbound lidocaine (mg/L)", "Total lidocaine (mg/L)", "AAG (umol/L)"),
  `Figure 4D, 72 h` = c(0.77, 4.65, 15.3),
  Simulated = c(d72$Cunbound, d72$Cc, d72$aag),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # Unbound plateau in Figure 4D; a wrong CL, F or dose moves it by tens of percent.
  abs(d72$Cunbound / 0.77 - 1) < 0.05,
  # AAG and total depend on the stimulus and turnover constants; Figure 4D
  # was read by eye, so the bound is wider.
  abs(d72$aag / 15.3 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(d72$Cc / 4.65 - 1) < 0.15,
  # Results text: about 1.3 h at 1 mg/kg/h and about 0.6 h at 2 mg/kg/h.
  abs(fig4_times$t_c50[fig4_times$rate_mgkgh == 1] / 1.3 - 1) < 0.35,
  abs(fig4_times$t_score5[fig4_times$rate_mgkgh == 2] / 0.6 - 1) < 0.35
)
```

# Visual predictive check (Figure 3)

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, time, arm, `Unbound lidocaine (mg/L)` = Cunbound, `Total lidocaine (mg/L)` = Cc, `Pain score (VAS cm)` = score) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, time, arm)) |>
  group_by(time, arm, name) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(value, 0.1),
    p50 = median(value),
    p90 = quantile(value, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(name ~ arm, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after lidocaine start (h)", y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Model predictions (median and 10th-90th percentiles, no residual error),",
      "cf. Figure 3 of Osborne 2025."
    )
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

Table 1 of the paper reports the observed Cmax (mean) and Tmax (median) over
the trial sampling times, so the NCA uses only those times (0.08-48 h).
Concentrations are individual predictions without residual error.

```{r pknca}
run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc <- sim |>
    filter(time %in% c(0, pk_times)) |>
    # The trial took no time-0 sample; the pre-dose concentration is 0.
    mutate(conc = if_else(time == 0, 0, .data[[conc_col]])) |>
    filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
    select(id, arm, time, conc)
  doses <- events |>
    filter(evid == 1, rate == 0) |>
    select(id, arm, time, amt)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | arm + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | arm + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 48, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_unbound <- run_nca("Cunbound")
nca_total <- run_nca("Cc")

summarise_nca <- function(res) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax")) |>
    group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(value = if (PPTESTCD[1] == "cmax") mean(PPORRES) else median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)
}
sim_unbound <- summarise_nca(nca_unbound)
sim_total <- summarise_nca(nca_total)
```

## Comparison against published Table 1

Simulated Cmax is the cohort **mean** and Tmax the cohort **median**, matching
how Table 1 summarises the observed data.

```{r nca-compare}
ref_unbound <- data.frame(arm = c("IP", "IV"), cmax = c(0.6, 0.8), tmax = c(48, 48))
ref_total <- data.frame(arm = c("IP", "IV"), cmax = c(3.1, 3.6), tmax = c(48, 48))

cmp <- bind_rows(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    sim_unbound, ref_unbound, by = "arm",
    units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h")
  ) |> mutate(Analyte = "Unbound"),
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    sim_total, ref_total, by = "arm",
    units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h")
  ) |> mutate(Analyte = "Total")
) |>
  relocate(Analyte)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. Osborne 2025 Table 1. * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

```{r nca-assert}
pct <- function(sim, ref) 100 * (sim / ref - 1)
stopifnot(
  # Unbound Cmax is set by dose, F and CL alone: a mis-transcribed clearance,
  # bioavailability or dose basis moves it by tens of percent. The cohort
  # means sit at about -17% (IP) and +7% (IV).
  abs(pct(sim_unbound$cmax[sim_unbound$arm == "IP"], 0.6)) < 30,
  abs(pct(sim_unbound$cmax[sim_unbound$arm == "IV"], 0.8)) < 30,
  # Total Cmax also carries the AAG time course (about +3% for IP). The IV
  # arm is a known deviation and is reported, not gated; see below.
  abs(pct(sim_total$cmax[sim_total$arm == "IP"], 3.1)) < 30,
  # Intraperitoneal concentrations rise throughout the infusion.
  sim_unbound$tmax[sim_unbound$arm == "IP"] == 48
)
```

Unbound Cmax in both arms and total Cmax in the intraperitoneal arm agree
with Table 1. In the intravenous arm, simulated total Cmax is about a third
above the observed 3.6 mg/L. The model's total-to-unbound ratio at 48 h is
about 6, against 3.6 / 0.8 = 4.5 in the observed intravenous means and
3.1 / 0.6 = 5.2 in the intraperitoneal means. That ratio is
`1 + aag / kaag`, and it rises with the AAG time course. The AAG sub-model
was fitted to paediatric data and never saw adult AAG, so the adult AAG rise
after surgery is an extrapolation. The observed means are also lowered by the
six patients (three per arm) whose infusion stopped early, and the comparison
depends on the assumed weights. The paper itself notes misfit in total
lidocaine (Figure 3, middle panels).

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Proportional residual errors.** In the NM-TRAN code each proportional
  theta multiplies `EPS(1)`, whose `$SIGMA` is 1 and held constant. The theta
  is therefore the proportional SD itself: 0.26 for unbound, 0.271 for total,
  0.462 for the pain score. Tables 2 and 3 print the square roots of these
  (51%, 52%, 68%), as though the thetas were variances. The additive SDs are
  printed unchanged (0.03, 0.04, 0.13). The model uses the code values. The AAG
  error in code 1 is a true `$SIGMA` variance (0.0372), so its SD is
  sqrt(0.0372).
- **PK IIV block held constant.** In code 1 the last element of the
  `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)` (TABS, CLU, V1, Q, V2) carries `FIX`. In NONMEM this holds
  the whole block constant, so the model wraps the block in `fixed()`. The
  variances equal the Table 2 %PPV values.
- **IIV fixed to zero.** Code 1 and code 2 declare several etas as `0 FIX`
  (on F, VIP, V_AAG, KD, the stimulus half-life and slope, the maturation Hill,
  E0, the drug Hill and the pain Emax). They contribute nothing and are
  omitted.
- **One model file for two NONMEM runs.** The PD run (code 2) fixed the PK
  thetas and omegas at the code 1 estimates. Code 2 holds the unbound
  proportional SD at 0.259, against 0.26 in code 1; the packaged model uses
  0.26. The AAG layer does not feed the pain score.
- **Surgical stimulus.** Methods Eq. 4 prints `SYN = CSTIMULUS * SLOPE`, but
  the code uses `SYN = 1 + SLOPE * CSTIMULUS`, which keeps baseline AAG
  production when the stimulus has decayed. The model follows the code. The
  stimulus clock is model time, so time 0 must be the start of surgery and of
  lidocaine, as in the trial.
- **Discussion vs. Table 2.** The Discussion quotes CLU as 118 L/h/70 kg.
  Table 2 and code 1 give 121 L/h/70 kg, which the model uses.
- **Figure 4 legend.** Under a constant infusion R, unbound lidocaine tends to
  `0.664 * R * 70 / 121` mg/L. The four concentration curves in Figure 4 A-B
  level off near 0.57, 0.75, 0.95 and 1.15 mg/L. Those match R = 1.5, 2, 2.5
  and 3 mg/kg/h, not the captioned 1-2.5 mg/kg/h. Panels C-D (2 mg/kg/h)
  agree with the model, so the vignette checks those panels and the Results
  text, not panels A-B.
- **Time to a 5-point pain reduction.** The paper reports 1.3 h at 1 mg/kg/h
  and about 36 min at 2 mg/kg/h, but does not say whether these are times to
  the 0.21 mg/L C50 or to a pain score of 5. The packaged model gives 1.5 h
  and 0.45 h to the C50, and 1.0 h and 0.5 h to a score of 5 (with
  `T_SURG = 0`). All of these are within about 30% of the paper.
- **Intravenous total Cmax.** The simulated mean total Cmax in the
  intravenous arm is about 33% above Table 1 (see the PKNCA comparison). This
  is reported and left out of the assertions. The parameters were not tuned.
- **Virtual cohort.** The paper reports no weight, height or sex. The cohort
  draws weight from N(80, 15) kg (truncated to 45-140 kg), height by sex, and
  50% female. Ideal body weight, which sets the dose, uses the Devine formula;
  the paper does not name its formula. The operative time `T_SURG` is set to
  3 h for all subjects and only affects the pain score.
- **Postmenstrual age.** The AAG maturation fraction is 1 for any adult.
  `PAGE` is set to 52.18 x age (years) + 40 weeks.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-05).
